On this page

  • How to use it
  1. Play with a band
  2. DAW

DAW

A small DAW as a scratch pad: tracks of drums, bass, keys and guitar on the band’s sounds, a piano roll and step grid, recording from the computer keys, MIDI or the microphone, a mixer, Session view and MIDI / WAV export. Kept in your browser.
Your work is kept in this browser. Save project downloads a copy; Reset clears it.

How to use it

  • Tracks. Pick an instrument and press + Track; × in a track’s header deletes it. + Clip makes a one-bar clip at the playhead; drag a clip to move it, its right edge to lengthen it.
  • Notes. Click a clip to open it below: a step grid for drums, a piano roll for the rest. Keys (or R to record) plays notes from the computer keyboard (A W S E D … ; Z / X change octave) or a MIDI keyboard.
  • Band. “Session players” writes drum, bass and keys parts for chords you type, as clips you can then edit.
  • Keeping it. Save project downloads a .json, Open project loads one; Export MIDI for another DAW, Bounce to WAV for an audio file.
  • Projects. The Project row at the top keeps several named projects: rename, switch, New, Duplicate, Delete. Copy / Paste (Ctrl/Cmd+C, X, V) put a clip at the playhead on the selected track, or selected notes into the open clip. Zoom − / + / Fit (Ctrl/Cmd + and −) for the arrangement and the roll.
  • Track sound. Under the editor, the selected track’s panel: an organ track has nine tonebars, Leslie, swell and key click (and Leslie → … / Swell here put automation points at the playhead); every track has three insert effects (EQ, compressor, distortion, amp, chorus, phaser, delay, reverb, tremolo, rotary, filter) and sends to a shared reverb and delay; the Synth: instruments (subtractive, FM, wavetable, chip pulse) have the patches from the Sound design lessons. Unchecked by ear.
  • Band row menus. Next to Style, Comping (piano or guitar), Rhythm (Charleston, Garland, four, bossa …) and Voicing override what the style would play; “Style default” leaves them alone. Press Write the parts again to hear the change.
  • Edit as notation. Select a note clip and open the panel under the editor: the clip as a staff and ABC text, quantised to sixteenths (or eighths), chords as [CEG]. Edit the text, then Apply: one Undo step; each note keeps its velocity if its pitch and start match. It warns first if notes are off the grid. Click a note on the staff to select it in the roll.
  • Fill from chords. Type chords (“Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7”), choose the bars (From / To, Loop, or Clip) and a source: a band style, a workstation arp type, or a Style Arranger section; Fill writes one clip on a new or chosen track (Undo takes it back). Chords from the selected clip reads them from the notation text or from the notes. Nobody has listened to these fills yet.
  • Step and keys. The Step menu (1/16, Beat, Bar) sizes keyboard moves. ← → move the playhead a step (Shift: a bar). Option+← → or h / l move the selected notes in the roll, else the selected clip, a step (Option+Shift or H / L: a bar); with nothing selected they move the playhead (Esc selects nothing). Option+↑ ↓ transpose selected notes (Shift: an octave). A number first repeats (“3l”). These replace Shift+arrow clip moves here.
  • Loop. Drag across the bar ruler to draw the loop (it snaps to the Step), drag its left or right handle to resize, drag the middle to move it, double-click a bar to loop that bar, click to put the playhead there. From the keyboard: , sets the loop start and . the loop end at the playhead, \ or O turns it on and off, Shift+O (or the “Loop clip” button) loops the selected clip.
  • Panels. Every part is a folding panel: click its name to fold it, drag its ⠿ grip to move it up, down or into a second column (a sidebar), or press ⇄ to send it across. The layout and what is folded are remembered; Reset layout puts everything back. Full screen (⛶) keeps the layout.
  • Go to a position. Click the position readout (or press G), type a bar, bar.beat or bar.beat.sixteenth (“6”, “6.3”, “6.1.4”), Enter to jump, Esc to cancel. It follows time-signature changes (a beat in 6/8 is a dotted quarter).
  • Each part is taught step by step in the DAW lessons, starting with DAW 1.
